title: Given a Scenario, Configure Switching Technologies and Features

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: Switches do more than connect devices. Learn how to segment traffic, configure interfaces, carry VLANs, combine links, prevent Layer 2 loops, and handle Ethernet frame sizes.
bullets: Native VLANs, voice VLANs, and 802.1Q tagging

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Given a switching scenario, identify how the switch should segment traffic, configure interfaces, prevent loops, and handle Ethernet frames.
bullets: Stored switch VLAN information → VLAN database
Logical Layer 3 interface for a VLAN → SVI
Separate IP phone VLAN → Voice VLAN
Physical links combined logically → Link aggregation

sections.title: VLANs, VLAN Databases, and SVIs

entries.title: Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN)
paragraphs: A VLAN logically separates devices into different Layer 2 networks even when they share physical switching infrastructure. Each VLAN is its own broadcast domain—for example, VLAN 10 users, VLAN 20 servers, and VLAN 30 printers.

entries.title: VLAN Database
paragraphs: The VLAN database stores the VLAN information configured on a switch. The switch must know which VLAN IDs exist before its ports can participate correctly in those VLANs.
entries.memoryHook: Which VLANs exist on this switch?

entries.title: Switch Virtual Interface (SVI)
paragraphs: An SVI is a logical Layer 3 interface associated with a VLAN. It can provide switch management or inter-VLAN routing on a capable switch. A VLAN 20 SVI might use 192.168.20.1.
entries.memoryHook: The VLAN gets an IP interface.

sections.callout: VLAN = Layer 2 segment. SVI = Layer 3 IP interface for that segment.

sections.title: Native VLAN, Voice VLAN, and 802.1Q

entries.title: Native VLAN
paragraphs: On an 802.1Q trunk, the native VLAN carries traffic that is normally untagged. Both ends of the trunk should agree on the native VLAN.

entries.title: Voice VLAN
paragraphs: A voice VLAN separates IP phone traffic from normal workstation data. The separation helps organization, security policy, and QoS implementation.
entries.memoryHook: Phone traffic gets its own VLAN.

entries.title: 802.1Q Tagging
paragraphs: IEEE 802.1Q inserts VLAN identification into Ethernet frames so one trunk can carry multiple VLANs.
entries.memoryHook: Which VLAN does this frame belong to?

sections.callout: Tagged multi-VLAN traffic → 802.1Q. Untagged trunk traffic → Native VLAN.

sections.title: Link Aggregation
paragraphs: Link aggregation combines multiple physical network links into one logical connection. It can increase aggregate bandwidth, provide redundancy, and distribute load.
sections.callout: Several physical switch links acting as one logical connection → Link aggregation.

entries.title: Speed
paragraphs: Speed is the configured transmission rate, such as 100 Mbps, 1 Gbps, or 10 Gbps. Interfaces can negotiate it or be configured manually.

entries.title: Duplex
paragraphs: Half duplex sends or receives but not simultaneously. Full duplex sends and receives simultaneously. A duplex mismatch can leave a link connected while causing unexpectedly poor performance.

sections.title: Spanning Tree
paragraphs: Redundant switch links improve availability but can create Layer 2 loops. Spanning tree builds a loop-free logical topology and can place redundant paths in a non-forwarding state until needed.
sections.callout: Redundant switch connections without a Layer 2 loop → Spanning tree.

sections.title: MTU and Jumbo Frames

entries.title: Maximum Transmission Unit (MTU)
paragraphs: MTU identifies the largest supported transmission size in a packet or frame context. MTU mismatches can cause communication and performance problems.

entries.title: Jumbo Frames
paragraphs: A jumbo frame is larger than a standard Ethernet frame. It can help some high-volume environments, but every participating device and link must support the configured size.

sections.callout: Size limit → MTU. Larger-than-standard Ethernet frame → Jumbo frame.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Separated IP phone traffic → Voice VLAN
Physical links acting as one → Link aggregation

entries.title: VLAN vs. SVI
paragraphs: Logical Layer 2 segment → VLAN. Logical Layer 3 interface for that VLAN → SVI.

entries.title: Native VLAN vs. Voice VLAN
paragraphs: Untagged trunk traffic → Native VLAN. IP phone traffic → Voice VLAN.

entries.title: Native VLAN vs. 802.1Q
paragraphs: Untagged VLAN on a trunk → Native VLAN. Tagged VLAN identification → 802.1Q.

entries.title: VLAN vs. 802.1Q
paragraphs: Logical segmentation → VLAN. Mechanism identifying VLAN traffic across tagged links → 802.1Q.

entries.title: Link Aggregation vs. Spanning Tree
paragraphs: Combine physical links logically → Link aggregation. Prevent Layer 2 loops → Spanning tree.

entries.title: Speed vs. Duplex
paragraphs: Transmission rate → Speed. Simultaneous send/receive capability → Full duplex.

entries.title: MTU vs. Jumbo Frame
paragraphs: Maximum transmission size → MTU. Larger-than-standard Ethernet frame → Jumbo frame.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Multiple links become one → Link aggregation
